text:
The evidence doesn't confirm deforestation. It does show a tree-cover loss candidate of about 13.5 ha (3.9% of the 345.6 ha property) mapped by Hansen/UMD in 2025.

- **Forest context:** JRC data show 98% of the loss area was forest in 2020. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 13.1 ha as native forest, none as planted, and 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest.
- **Status:** Pending corroboration. 2025 is the latest year in the series, so there is no later year to show whether the change persisted.
- **Limits:** Hansen loss counts any stand replacement, so it can't establish deforestation or land-use change. It also says nothing about cause (harvest, fire, storm or clearing), legality, or who was responsible.

In short, native forest tree-cover loss in 2025 is plausible, but calling it deforestation would need follow-up. That means a later year of imagery and some information on cause.
